state:
**Goal `ldap`, Stage 10 (the feature proofs): every `Core\Ldap` check but one passes.** Stages 1 to 5 and 7 to 9 are done. Stage 4 lacks only a CA a program supplies, and Stage 6 lacks only wiring the schema into the readers. `bun nv proofs --owed --limit 1000 | grep -i ldap` prints nothing. Every `bun nv proofs --verify --group 'Core\Ldap…'` check in `data/goals/ldap.json` passes, and so does the plain-comments check.

**`LdapError`, `ErrorKind`, `Tls`, `Scope` and `Ad\AccountType` have their proofs** under `docs/examples/types/Ldap-*/` and `tests/hostile/types/Ldap-LdapError/`. Their tests are `covers:` markers on existing `.nvst` cases. Their grants are `[[app]] root` entries in `nvs.toml`. A root must name a directory that exists, or every program fails with `E0605`.

**The `changes` attack loops twenty times, not a hundred** (playbook, *Writing a test case*). It now takes 14 to 23 s of its 120 s limit.

**The one red check is `dossier-the-whole-roster-owes-nothing-with-core-ldap`**, which runs `bun nv proofs --gate` and wants `nothing owed in the whole roster`. The roster owes 153 features outside this goal: 39 `Core\Str` (stale perf), about 60 `Core\Db`, `Core\Uuid`, `Core\Process`, `Core\Request` and many `lang:types/*`. **This needs the user.** One option is to narrow the check to the `Core\Ldap` features, for example by adding a `--group` for each `Core\Ldap` class to `--gate`. The other is to keep the check and close the other debt here. No session changed the check.

**Samba is slow and drops connections.** A huge filter, cookie or `select` makes Samba close the connection, and every later call on it throws `Unavailable`. An attack puts such a step last and catches every call. The proofs runner runs at most two `requires: samba-ad` programs at once.
